tossups.text: One essay about this adjective posits that "when we are no longer light-footed we find a place for ourselves in the band" and explains the leisure activities best suited for this type of people as fashion and gambling, using a Chinese anecdote about Wen Wang. That essay defines this adjective as the preference for "the limited to the unbounded, the near to the distant, the sufficient to the superabundant, the convenient to the perfect, present laughter to Utopian bliss." Another work with this adjective in the title states of it that "by its very nature it cannot offer an alternative to the direction in which we are moving," and that it lacks principle, does not understand economics, and has a fondness for authority. For 10 points, identify this word which appears in a Michael Oakeshott text about "being" one and a component of The Constitution of Liberty by Friedrich Hayek entitled "Why I Am Not" one of these.

This man's government gained the support of Francois Duke of Anjou after the signing of the Treaty of Plessis-les-Tours. He lost two of his brothers in the decisive defeat at Mookerheyde and in the court of Margaret of Parma, he became the leader of a faction called "The Beggars." This man had an illegitimate son with Eva Elincx, and that son Justinus became the admiral who handed over the keys of Breda to Ambrogio Spinola. He was assassinated by Balthasar Gerard and his government had earlier countered the formation of the Union of Arras by joining Holland and Zeeland in the Union of Utrecht. For 10 points, identify this man who organized the Dutch revolt against the rule of Philip II of Spain, and who is known as the "Father of the Netherlands."

Euclid's second postulate says that these mathematical objects can be created by extending another type of object, both of which he described as "breadthless." In three-dimensional space, these objects are skew if they fail to intersect but don't lie in the same plane. For ten points, name this one-dimensional geometric figure that, unlike a ray or segment, extends infinitely in both directions.

According to Joseph Smith, this is the only Biblical figure still alive. Tertullian said this man was boiled alive in oil but survived, after which he was banished to an island where he wrote a text that opened with an address to seven churches. With Peter and James, this man often described as "of Patmos" witnessed Jesus at the transubstantiation. At his crucifixion, Jesus told Mary this man was "her son." This apostle wrote the only non-synoptic gospel. For 10 points, name this apostle who wrote the book of Revelation, as well as the fourth Gospel.

This man convinced Omar Bongo to convert to Islam while on a visit. Two American GIs were killed after this leader ordered the bombing of a West Berlin discotheque. In a 2003 deal to lift sanctions, this leader accepted responsibility for sponsoring the Lockerbie bombing. This leader attacked both American and Soviet imperialism and advocated pan-Arab unity in his Green Book. This leader was deposed when rebels took his hometown of Sirte ("surt"). For 10 points, name this longtime dictator who was killed in 2011 by rebel militia in his home country of Libya.

This company's founder preceded it with the South Improvement Company, which attempted to collude with three major railroads to fix rates. One political cartoon depicted this company as a two-headed snake featuring protectionist Nelson Aldrich and this company's founder being strangled by Teddy Roosevelt. A better-known cartoon depicted this organization holding the steel and copper interests, as well as congress and the White House, in its tentacles. A major work on this company was serialized in McClure's Magazine and was written by Ida Tarbell. For 10 points what company was forced to dissolve in 1911, creating companies like Chevron and Mobil, founded by John D. Rockefeller?

Concerns over a forerunner of this law were investigated by attorney Samuel Untermyer as part of an inquiry by the Pujo Committee. This law's bill was introduced in the House by Robert Owen and Carter Glass, while a draft version of this law known as the "Aldrich Plan" is believed to have been conceived during a meeting at the Jekyll Island Club. This law, created in response to concerns about a "money trust," was modified in 1933 to create the FOMC, while another amendment in 1977 gave the result of this law a "dual mandate." The passage of this law came five years after the establishment of the National Monetary Commission, created to survey international banking systems after the Panic of 1907. For 10 points, name this bill signed by Woodrow Wilson, a 1913 Act that created the United States' current central bank.

In perfume, ethanol plays this role as a substance. When liquid, these can be distilled to leave a residue. Water is considered a "universal" one of these. This half of a solution typically has more volume than its counterpart. For 10 points, name these substances in which a solute is dissolved.

A binding partner of this protein is targeted by autoantibodies in a paraneoplastic form of stiff person syndrome found in breast cancer patients. This protein is inhibited by Pitstop1 and Pitstop2. This protein was originally isolated from pig and bollock brains by Barbara Pearse. This protein forms a complex with TACC and ch-TOG to stabilize the mitotic spindle apparatus. LDL receptor complexes localize to regions of the membrane containing this protein, which are PIP2-dependent structures called coated pits. Amphiphysin, epsin and AP180 are binding partners of this protein, which can also bind to the AP2 adaptor complex. Three heavy chains and three light chains of this protein are used to form a particular repeating structure. Dynamin is used to pinch off structures coated with this protein, which move from the cell membrane to the endosome in endocytosis. For 10 points, name this protein that forms a triskelion structure on the external surface of endocytic vesicles.

To produce these species, diazo dyes are most often paired with EDTA. A starch solution serves this role in iodometry when it bonds to triiodide. The presence of anthocyanins in certain cauliflower and red cabbage extracts allow them to be used as natural types of these things. One of these substances that has a large effective range is its "universal" kind, and is made by mixing several others containing thymol and bromothymol groups. In a back titration, one of these substances is added to the analyte, causing the analyte to appear pink until the equivalence point; that one of these things is phenolphthalein. For 10 points, name these substances which change color as a reaction progresses, often signifying a change in pH.

Roland Mitchell fails to get a get a job in this profession at the beginning of A. S. Byatt's Possession, losing the job to the charming Fergus Wolff. The title character of a novel by Kingsley Amis loses his job in this profession after performing it drunkenly and speaking at length about "Merrie England." One character with this day job, along with his detective rival, dies after falling off Reichenbach Falls in The Adventure of the Final Problem. David Lurie in J.M. Coatzee's Disgrace loses this job after an illicit affair with a student. Sherlock Holmes's rival Moriarty has, for 10 points, what academic job?
acceptableAnswers: math professor but not other more specific types of professors

tossups.text: Sophocles is reminded of human misery in the second stanza of this poem when he hears the eternal note of sadness on the Aegean. The world hath neither joy nor love nor light for the speaker even though the sea is calm tonight. The speaker and his love are on a darkling plain where ignorant armies clash by night in, for 10 points, what poem which takes place on the cliffs of England, overlooking the French coast, a poem by Matthew Arnold.

In 2014, Dutch students Kris Kremers and Lisanne Froon were found dead in this country after hiking the "Pianist" trail near Boquete. That trail is located in Chiriquí province, which contains this nation's highest point, Barú Volcano. Thomas Drummond attempted to found the colony of Caledonia in a region of this country which is navigated using piragua boats and has prevented the spread of foot-and-mouth disease to this country. The Chagres river flows into this country's manmade Lake Gatun, which is utilised by a structure that connects Balboa on the Pacific and Colon on the Caribbean Sea. Sharing the Darién Gap with Colombia, for 10 points, name this Central American nation which has a namesake Canal.

An "American" example of these objects depicting everyday life was created by artist Sandow Birk. The Bardo National Museum houses most of one of these objects dyed in indigo and decorated with gold, called the "Blue" one. A 2016 exhibit at the Sackler Gallery on the "art of" these things showed one of them commissioned by Uljaytu that exemplifies muhaqqaq style. The ghusam technique was used by Omar Aqta to create one of these objects in the form of a signet ring for Timur. The decorated margins of many of these objects often indicate juz' divisions. These are the most common objects to be made using decorative Kufic ("KOO-fick") script. Doctrinal aniconism ("an-EYE-kon-ism") prompted hilya artists to use elaborate calligraphy to depict the man who revealed this book. For 10 points, name this book whose prophetic revealer cannot be depicted visually according to orthodox Islam.
acceptableAnswers: accept The Art of the Qur’an

tossups.text: The protagonist ‟s grandson, Niou [nee-oh], and his wife ‟s illegitimate son, Kaoru [kah-oh- roo], pursue three sisters in the last third of this novel, after the title figure ‟s death. This novel ‟s protagonist is briefly exiled to Suma by the emperor, his illegitimate son. A friend of Tō no Chūjō [toh noh choo-joh] raises Fujitsubo's [foo-jee-tsoo-boh's] niece to be the perfect wife for the title "shining" Japanese prince in this novel. For 10 points, name this early novel by Murasaki Shikibu [moo-rah-sah-kee shee-kee-boo].

This character develops lifelong stomach troubles after being forced to eat an entire bunch of bananas as a punishment for stealing. This character burns his shop down for insurance money as part of his resolution to "paddle his own canoe." After this character gets distracted while watching a calf, his father drowns in a stream. This author of several stories titled "Escape" interviews many "Deserving Destitutes" for the Sentinel newspaper. This man, who lives with his wife Shama at the Hanuman House with the Tulsi family after stopping working as a sign painter, dies young while still owing a mortgage on the title structure. For 10 points, V. S. Naipaul ("NYE-paul") wrote a novel about a "house" for what character?
acceptableAnswers: accept A House for Mr. Biswas

tossups.text: Due to its premiere in a library, a ballet by this composer was originally scored for a thirteen-piece chamber orchestra. A choreographer transcribed "I Ride an Old Paint" for a ballet by this composer whose finale quotes "Bonaparte's Retreat." A solo clarinet introduces the theme of a Doppio Movimento movement by this composer that uses the same melody as "Lord of the Dance." A preacher, the Bride, and her Intended are the main characters of a ballet by this composer whose score contains five variations on "Simple Gifts." Another of his ballets ends with a "Hoe-Down." For 10 points, name this queer Jewish-American composer of Rodeo ("ro-DAY-oh") and Appalachian Spring.

During flashbacks the main character remembers his time as the creator of "a field of fire," while his mother feigns mental illness and wants to kill the leader of the "blue tunics," Ben Wackes. This eventually causes her to steal a pistol from her gardener and shoot the wrong man. Taking place over ten hours on September 6, 1958, much of it is dominated by opposing mentalities symbolized by the "lamb" and "buffalo." The latter is represented by Otto, who died near Kiev, while the protagonist's childhood friend, Alfred Schrella, represents the former and returns from exile late in the novel. Its title refers to the protagonist's appointment with the bellboy Hugo at the Prince Heinrich Hotel and much of the story is taken up with the mystery about the destruction of the central family's masterpiece, St. Anthony's Abbey. Ultimately Joseph finds out that his own father demolished it. For 10 points identify this work narrated by Robert Fahmel, a man who likes to escape his past by playing the title game in a work by Heinrich Boll.

A character in this book is about to be executed, but a birthmark that resembles a bloody arrow under his shoulder reveals him to be the son of a priest. Another character in this book recounts how he got a big-ass sword when a dying hermit near Joppa instructed him to dig underneath the seventh tree to the left of a cave. It was supposedly translated into English by William Marshall, based off of the original work of Onuphrio Muralto. This work opens on the wedding day of Isabella and Conrad, who is killed by a falling helmet. Father Jerome's son ends up marrying the daughter of the Knight of the Gigantic Sabre in this novel, who possesses a sword with an inscription demanding the blood of Manfred to atone for his sins. For 10 points, identify this early Gothic novel by Horace Walpole.

Orpheus was killed by this god's followers, who were known as the maenads, and this god turned a crew of pirates who tried to abduct him into dolphins. After this god's mother, Semele, died after looking at Zeus in his true form, this god was sown into Zeus' thigh. Hestia gave up her throne on Mount Olympus in favor of, for 10 points, what Greek counterpart of Bacchus, the god of wine?

parts.text: Primarily developed by Yoruba slaves in Cuba, it blends West African beliefs with Roman Catholicism.
This is the term for the system of divination that allows Santeria priests to understand the teachings of the various Orisha or spirits.
The many Orishas are actually different manifestations of this Supreme Being of the Yoruba spiritual system.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a religion also known as Lukumi, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this event that many New Englanders interpreted as the Day of Judgement. This event caused Mother Ann Lee's Shakers to begin preaching publicly.
The most likely explanation for the Dark Day of 1780 is that it was caused by one of these events. Another of these events in Chicago was supposedly started by a cow owned by Catherine O'Leary.
One record of the Dark Day comes from this letter writer's correspondence with James Lovell. A proposal by this writer was met with a response that it would create a "despotism of the petticoat."

parts.text: Name this English naturalist, who studied finches on the Galapagos Islands and introduced the theory of natural selection.
Darwin's best known work is this one, in which he put forth his theory of natural selection, along with other thoughts and ideas on evolution.

Darwin's ideas expanded on the work of this French naturalist, who was a proponent of inheritance of acquired characteristics. According to this man's theories, if a man works out and his muscles get larger, that largeness of muscle will be passed on genetically.

bonuses.leadin: He wrote the book, The Descent of Man and sailed on the HMS Beagle. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this syncretic religion prominent in Haiti and Louisiana, whose practitioners only rarely stick pins into dolls.
The distant Voodoo god Bondye communicates with mankind through this group of spirits. Members of this group include Papa Legba, Maman Brigette, and the skeletal Baron Samedi.
This other syncretized religion borrowed practices from the Yoruba people and combined them with Roman Catholicism. Its Orisha spirits serve as manifestations of the god Olorun.

bonuses.leadin: In this religion, male priests are houngans and female priests are mambos. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this political entity, many members of which use the Euro and maintain the Schengen Area.
The current structure of the EU was formed by a 1993 treaty named for this Dutch city.
The EU arose from a supranational European "community" for trading these two commodities.

bonuses.leadin: Nations may enter this organization if they fulfill the Copenhagen Criteria. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this editorial cartoonist who died in 2001 and was often known by just one name.
Herblock was also known for cartoons depicting this Senator from Wisconsin, who believed that Communists had infiltrated the United States federal government.
Herblock worked for this newspaper for over fifty years. Bob Woodward and Carl Bernstein helped this newspaper win a Pulitzer Prize in 1973 for its Watergate investigation.

bonuses.leadin: This man received a Pulitzer Prize in 1954 for a work in which Joseph Stalin is being led to his grave by Death, who says "You Were Always A Great Friend of Mine." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this female prime minister of India who was assassinated in 1984. She was the daughter of India's first prime minister, Jawaharlal Nehru.

Indira Gandhi was assassinated shortly after ordering Operation Blue Star, in which the Indian army entered this city, angering adherents of a certain religion and probably fueling her murder by her own bodyguards.
In 1974, during Indira Gandhi's ministry, India successfully detonated a nuclear bomb for the first time during a test commonly known by this two-word English name.

bonuses.leadin: Richard Nixon called this leader both a "clever fox" and a "witch". For 10 points each:

parts.text: This part of the brain contains the four lobes and the two halves are separated by the central sulcus. It has been estimated that it has a surface area of 1.3 square feet due to the numerous folds in this structure.
This lobe contains the Broca's area and is responsible for decision-making and conscious thought. It is separated from the parietal lobes by the primary motor cortex.
The cerebral cortex is mostly made up by this substance that contains mostly neural cell bodies instead of myelinated axon tracts that gives it a distinctive color.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about a particular part of the brain, for 10 points each.

parts.text: Name this entity corresponding to a partition function equal to the sum over states and particle numbers, N, of a constant z to the N times the exponential of minus the state energy over kinetic temperature, kT.

The aforementioned factor z in the partition function of the grand canonical ensemble is equal to this quantity, which is equal to the exponential of the chemical potential, mu, over kT and measures the difficulty in adding a particle to the ensemble.

For the grand canonical ensemble, this quantity is given by the pressure times the volume, as can be shown by performing an N-to-mu Legendre transform of the form of this quantity applicable to the canonical ensemble and considering that volume is then the only extensive variable.

bonuses.leadin: This idealization consists of an arbitrarily large number of initially identical chemical systems that are free to exchange heat and particles with a reservoir. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this embryonic developmental process of several rapid cell divisions in the absence of cell growth. During it, the zygote turns into the morula, then the blastula.
In humans, embryonic cleavage partitions the blastula into two poles: one yolk-rich and one yolk-poor, the latter eventually forming the germ layers. Name both poles.

Human embryos undergo holoblastic cleavage, in which very little yolk is left in the egg. That's because human embryos are nourished by this organ, which connects the developing fetus to the mother's uterus.

bonuses.leadin: This process occurs radially in deuterostomes like vertebrates and echinoderms. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Epics such as the Lusiads and the Odyssey begin in this manner. Horace coined this three-word term, meaning "in the middle of things," in his Ars Poetica.

Epic poetry is also characterized by the frequent use of the "Homeric" variety of these literary devices. These literary devices differ from metaphors in that they use the words "like" or "as" to compare two things.
Epic poetry often uses stock ones of these phrases. Examples of these phrases used in the Iliad include "rosy-fingered" and "swift footed."

parts.text: Name this tributary of the Mississippi that rises from the confluence of the Allegheny and Monongahela Rivers at Pittsburgh and flows past Cincinnati in its namesake state.
This largest tributary of the Ohio River is formed from the confluence of the French Broad and Holston Rivers just outside of Knoxville and creates a namesake valley in northern Alabama.
This tributary of the Ohio is the principal river of Indiana, whose cities of Terre Haute and Vincennes lie on its course.

parts.text: Teinosuke Kinugasa was one of the best-known directors in an era named for what kind of film? In the U.S., these films became less popular with the advent of "talkies" such as The Jazz Singer.
This actor made a cameo appearance in The Picture Bride as a benshi travelling in Hawaii. This actor played the ronin Sanjuro in Akira Kurosawa's Yojimbo.

Contemporary benshi Midori Sawato has narrated many silent films featuring this Japanese Hollywood star, such as The Dragon Painter, for Japanese audiences. Despite Hays code restrictions on his romantic roles, he was wildly popular, and later starred as Colonel Saito in the "talkie" The Bridge on the River Kwai.
acceptableAnswers: accept either name in reverse order

parts.text: Name this author of Gypsy Ballads who wrote of the strong-willed title character and her daughters in The House of Bernarda Alba.
García Lorca was shot during this country's civil war and wrote a lament for one of its bullfighters. Miguel de Unamuno was part of this country's Generation of 98.
Jose Saramago, who told of an epidemic of the title condition in Blindness, is an author from this other Iberian nation.

parts.text: Name this work in which the goddess "Dulness" conquers England and declares a need to control the dramatic, political, and religious poetry of England.
The author of The Dunciad wrote this work dedicated to Arabella Fermor, in which the Baron performs the title action as he cuts Belinda's hair.
This author of The Dunciad and The Rape of the Lock wrote Eloisa to Abelard as well as an Essay on Man.

This man composed Winterreise. He also composed Rosamunde, Death and the Miser and a noted Unfinished Symphony.
This work is feature in Vikram Seth's An Equal Music, and was created out of Die Forelle. This quintet is named for a fish.

In The Finkler Question, Treslove used to work for this organisation. The name of a fictional town in a literary work written for this organisation was created by reversing the phrase "bugger all."
In 2010, The Finkler Question won this annual award for best English language novel. The shortlist for the 2023 edition of this award featured three authors with the forename Paul.

parts.text: Name this ancient city that served as capital for Hammurabi and Nebuchadnezzar in two different empires named for it.

Nebuchadnezzar ordered the creation of this Babylonian structure, the only one of the seven ancient Wonders of the World whose location and existence hasn't been completely confirmed. This structure may have featured stacked terraces of plants and wildlife.
Babylon was located along the banks of this river that, along with its companion the Tigris River, was the source of water for much of Mesopotamia.
